# Posit Connect Cloud {#sec-posit-connect-cloud} :::: {.callout-note collapse='true' appearance='default' icon=false} ## [TLDR: Deploying to Connect Cloud]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.05em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 0.95em;'} [Posit Connect Cloud](https://posit.cloud/) is a managed hosting platform for deploying Shiny applications, Quarto documents, and other R/Python content. Deploy your app-package using `rsconnect::deployApp()` with your Connect Cloud account credentials. The deployment process is identical to shinyapps.io but gives you a centralized platform integrated with your Posit Team workspace. 1. Create a [Posit Connect Cloud](https://posit.cloud/) account and note your server URL 2. Install and configure `rsconnect` with your account credentials 3. Deploy using `rsconnect::deployApp()` from RStudio or Positron 4. Monitor your application through the Connect Cloud dashboard ::: :::: This chapter covers deploying your app-package to [Posit Connect Cloud](https://posit.cloud/), a managed hosting platform for Shiny applications and other content. Unlike shinyapps.io, Connect Cloud integrates directly with your Posit Team workspace, giving you a centralized place to manage all your deployed applications alongside your collaborators' work. We deployed the production version of our application in @sec-resources-prod-deploy, but here I'll walk through the Connect Cloud deployment workflow and show you what to expect during and after deployment. ::::{.callout-tip collapse='true' appearance='deafult'} ## [Access the applications in this chapter]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.15em;'} :::{style='font-size: 0.95em;'} I've created the [`shinypak` R package](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/shinypak/) in an effort to make each section accessible and easy to follow. Install `shinypak` using `pak` (or `remotes`): ```r install.packages('pak') pak::pak('mjfrigaard/shinypak') library(shinypak) ``` List the apps in this chapter: ```r list_apps(regex = '^19') ``` Launch apps with `launch()` ```r launch(app = '19_connect-cloud') ``` Download apps with `get_app()` ```r get_app(app = '19_connect-cloud') ``` :::: ::: ## Deployment workflow {#sec-connect-cloud-workflow} The diagram below shows the complete deployment flow from your local development environment to a running application in Connect Cloud: ```{mermaid} %%| eval: true %%| fig-align: 'center' %%| fig-caption: 'Posit Connect Cloud deployment workflow' %%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "fontSize":"14px", "darkMode":true}}}}%% flowchart TD subgraph Local["Local Development"] code["App-package code
(R/, inst/, app.R)"] test["Test locally with
launch_app()"] end subgraph Config["Configuration"] creds["rsconnect credentials
(API key, server URL)"] end subgraph Deploy["Deployment"] bundle["Bundle files &

Install and load it: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} install.packages("rsconnect") library(rsconnect) ``` ::: Connect Cloud uses API authentication, which means you'll configure `rsconnect` with your server URL and API key (not a username and password). You can generate an API key from your Connect Cloud account settings. Set your Connect Cloud credentials using `rsconnect::connectUser()`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} rsconnect::connectUser( account = "https://connect.posit.cloud", token = "your_api_key", server = "posit-connect-cloud" ) ``` ::: Once configured, `rsconnect` will remember your credentials for future deployments. ### Deploying from RStudio ![](images/rstudio-icon.png){height=20} RStudio connects to Connect Cloud through the **Publish** button. After configuring your account, load and document your app-package, then launch `app.R`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} devtools::load_all() devtools::document() source("app.R") ``` ::: Click the **Publish** icon in the **Viewer** pane, select your deployment account, choose which files to include, and enter an app name. RStudio will bundle your files and send them to Connect Cloud. ### Deploying from Positron ![](images/positron.png){height=20} You can also deploy from Positron ![](images/positron.png){height=20} using the `rsconnect::deployApp()` function. This approach gives you full control over deployment parameters: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="false"} rsconnect::deployApp( appDir = getwd(), appName = "movie-reviews", server = "posit-connect-cloud", account = "your_account") ``` ::: The deployment output is printed directly to the **Console**, and the process works identically to RStudio's **Publish** button—both use `rsconnect` under the hood. ## Deployment logs {#sec-connect-cloud-deploy-logs} When you deploy to Connect Cloud, you'll see output showing each step of the process: bundling files, capturing dependencies, uploading the bundle, and building the container environment. Here's what a successful deployment looks like: ```{.default} ── Preparing for deployment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── ℹ Deploying to Posit Connect Cloud ℹ Creating application on server... ℹ Created deployment with id 98765432 ℹ Bundling 68 files: .Rbuildignore, app.R, DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, README.md, renv.lock, inst/extdata/movies.fst, inst/prod/app/app.R, R/launch_app.R, R/mod_var_input.R, R/mod_scatter_display.R, R/scatter_plot.R, data/movies.rda, man/*.Rd, tests/testthat/*.R, and others... ℹ Capturing R dependencies ℹ Found 87 dependencies ℹ Created 2,941,205b bundle ℹ Uploading bundle... ✔ Uploaded bundle ── Deploying to server ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ℹ Waiting for deployment to start... ℹ Building image... ℹ Installing system dependencies... ℹ Installing R packages... ℹ Starting deployment... ✔ Deployment succeeded! ℹ Your application is available at: https://your-workspace.connect.posit.cloud/content/abc123/ ``` The bundling step captures all your R dependencies through `renv.lock` (if you're using `renv`) or by scanning your code for package imports. Connect Cloud then builds a container image with those dependencies installed, ensuring your app runs the same way regardless of updates to external packages. You can monitor your application's status and view more detailed logs through the Connect Cloud dashboard. ## Monitoring and managing your application {#sec-connect-cloud-management} After your application is deployed, visit the Connect Cloud dashboard to monitor its status. You can view: - **Application logs**: Review startup messages and runtime output to debug issues. - **Usage metrics**: See how many users are accessing your app and when. - **Resource usage**: Monitor CPU and memory consumption. - **Deployment history**: Track previous versions and rollback if needed. You can also update your application by redeploying from RStudio or Positron—Connect Cloud will bundle the new code and replace the running instance with the updated version. ## The `rsconnect` folder {#sec-connect-cloud-rsconnect-dir} When you deploy with `rsconnect`, a `rsconnect/` folder is automatically created to store deployment metadata and configuration. This folder records which account and server each app was deployed to: ```{.default} rsconnect/ └── connect.posit.cloud └── your_account └── movie-reviews.dcf 3 directories, 1 file ``` The `.dcf` file contains metadata about your deployment (app ID, account, version), but it should **not** be committed to Git. It contains machine-specific settings and can cause conflicts when multiple team members deploy the same app. Add `rsconnect/` to `.gitignore` to prevent accidental commits: ```ini .Rproj.user .Rhistory .RData .Ruserdata .DS_Store sap.Rcheck/ sap*.tar.gz sap*.tgz rsconnect/ /.quarto/ inst/doc *_.new.png ``` If `rsconnect/` was already committed, remove it from Git history: ::: {.cell} ```{.bash .cell-code code-fold="false"} git rm -r --cached rsconnect/ git commit -m "Remove rsconnect folder from repository" git push origin main ``` ::: This will remove it from the Git history while keeping it locally. If we need to share deployment details with our team, we can document the deployment process in the `README.Rmd` or create a `deploy.Rmd` vignette. ## Recap {.unnumbered} Deploying your app-package to Posit Connect Cloud is straightforward: configure `rsconnect` with your account credentials, then push your app from RStudio or Positron. Connect Cloud handles dependency management and container setup automatically. :::: {.callout-tip collapse='false' appearance='default' icon=false} ## [Recap: Posit Connect Cloud]{style='font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.05em;'} ::: {style='font-size: 0.95em;'} 1. Create a [Posit Connect Cloud](https://posit.cloud/) account and generate an API key from your account settings. 2. Install `rsconnect` and configure it with your Connect Cloud URL and API key using `rsconnect::connectUser()`. 3. Verify your app runs locally using `launch_app()` before deploying. 4. Deploy from RStudio using the **Publish** button or from any IDE using `rsconnect::deployApp()`. 5. Add `rsconnect/` to `.gitignore` to prevent deployment metadata from being committed: ```ini rsconnect/ ``` If already committed: ```sh git rm -r --cached rsconnect/ git commit -m 'Remove rsconnect folder from repository' ``` 6. Monitor your application through the Connect Cloud dashboard to view logs, usage, and manage versions. ::: ::::
